questionText: What is the primary difference between 'let', 'const', and 'var' in modern JavaScript (ES6+)?
options: 'let' and 'const' are block-scoped and temporal dead zone aware, whereas 'var' is function-scoped and hoisted with undefined
'var' cannot be reassigned once initialized
'const' creates immutable deep objects that prevent object key modification
'let' is only available inside browser Web Workers
correctAnswer: 'let' and 'const' are block-scoped and temporal dead zone aware, whereas 'var' is function-scoped and hoisted with undefined
explanation: 'let' and 'const' respect lexical block scopes ({ ... }) and cannot be accessed before declaration, unlike function-scoped 'var'.

questionText: In React, what is the consequence of modifying state directly via `this.state.count = 5` or mutating state variables without setter functions?
options: React will not trigger a re-render because it relies on setter functions to schedule reconciliation updates
The browser will immediately throw an uncaught ReferenceError
The database server will abort the current HTTP request
All child components are immediately unmounted from the DOM
correctAnswer: React will not trigger a re-render because it relies on setter functions to schedule reconciliation updates
explanation: Direct mutation bypasses React's state management lifecycle, so the Virtual DOM diffing algorithm is never scheduled to re-render the UI.

questionText: In Spring Boot, which annotation is used on a class to define REST endpoints that automatically serialize return values to JSON?
options: @RestController
@Controller
@Service
@Repository
correctAnswer: @RestController
explanation: @RestController is a convenience convenience annotation combining @Controller and @ResponseBody, serializing returned objects directly into HTTP response bodies.

questionText: What HTTP response status code should be returned when a resource is successfully created via a POST request?
options: 201 Created
200 OK
204 No Content
202 Accepted
correctAnswer: 201 Created
explanation: HTTP 201 Created indicates the request succeeded and resulted in the creation of one or more new resources, usually returning a Location header.

questionText: In PostgreSQL, which index type is the default when creating an index on a column?
options: B-Tree
Hash
GIN (Generalized Inverted Index)
BRIN (Block Range Index)
correctAnswer: B-Tree
explanation: PostgreSQL defaults to B-Tree indexes, which efficiently handle equality and range queries (<, <=, =, >=, >) on sortable data.

questionText: In React, what is the primary purpose of the `useEffect` hook's dependency array `[dep1, dep2]`?
options: It instructs React to re-execute the effect only when one of the specified dependencies changes between renders
It binds Redux store dispatchers to the component
It caches the return value in browser localStorage
It prevents the component from rendering more than once
correctAnswer: It instructs React to re-execute the effect only when one of the specified dependencies changes between renders
explanation: The dependency array allows React to skip re-running the effect on renders where none of the specified values have changed.

questionText: Which CSS property and value enables a flex container to arrange its children in a column and center them horizontally?
options: display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center;
display: flex; flex-direction: row; justify-content: center;
display: block; text-align: center; margin: auto;
display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr;
correctAnswer: display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center;
explanation: In column direction, the cross-axis is horizontal; therefore `align-items: center` centers items horizontally across the cross-axis.

questionText: In SQL, what is the key difference between `WHERE` and `HAVING` clauses?
options: `WHERE` filters individual rows before grouping; `HAVING` filters aggregated group records after `GROUP BY`
`WHERE` works only on text columns; `HAVING` works only on numbers
`HAVING` can only be used with subqueries
`WHERE` cannot be used with `JOIN` operations
correctAnswer: `WHERE` filters individual rows before grouping; `HAVING` filters aggregated group records after `GROUP BY`
explanation: WHERE filters rows prior to aggregation, while HAVING filters the results of aggregate expressions (SUM, COUNT, AVG) after grouping.

questionText: What does the JavaScript event loop do when an asynchronous Promise resolves?
options: Places the Promise callback into the Microtask Queue to be executed before the next Macrotask
Immediately interrupts synchronous execution on the call stack
Pushes the callback to a background thread in the operating system
Restarts the browser's JavaScript engine
correctAnswer: Places the Promise callback into the Microtask Queue to be executed before the next Macrotask
explanation: Resolved Promises are enqueued in the high-priority microtask queue, which is emptied immediately after the current call stack clears.

questionText: In Spring Data JPA, what does the `@Transactional` annotation guarantee on a service method?
options: That all database operations within the method execute inside a database transaction, rolling back on unhandled exceptions
That the endpoint is secured with JWT tokens
That HTTP requests are cached in Redis
That the method executes asynchronously on a separate thread pool
correctAnswer: That all database operations within the method execute inside a database transaction, rolling back on unhandled exceptions
explanation: @Transactional defines the scope of a single database transaction, ensuring ACID compliance and rolling back on runtime exceptions.

questionText: What vulnerability occurs when an application renders untrusted user input directly into HTML without sanitization?
options: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
Denial of Service (DoS)
correctAnswer: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
explanation: XSS allows attackers to inject malicious scripts into trusted websites, executing in victim browsers and stealing cookies or tokens.

questionText: In React, why must list elements have a unique `key` prop when mapped dynamically?
options: To help React's reconciliation algorithm identify which items were changed, added, or removed efficiently
To provide accessibility labels for screen readers
To automatically apply CSS styles to list items
To persist item data to IndexedDB
correctAnswer: To help React's reconciliation algorithm identify which items were changed, added, or removed efficiently
explanation: Keys give stable identity to Virtual DOM elements, preventing unnecessary DOM re-creations and state bugs during list mutations.

questionText: Which HTTP header is sent by servers to instruct browsers which origins are permitted to access resources via XMLHttpRequest or fetch?
options: Access-Control-Allow-Origin
Content-Security-Policy
X-Frame-Options
Authorization
correctAnswer: Access-Control-Allow-Origin
explanation: Access-Control-Allow-Origin is the foundational CORS header specifying allowed requesting origins (* or specific domain).

questionText: In modern CSS, what does `box-sizing: border-box` do?
options: Includes padding and border within the specified element width and height
Adds a black border around every HTML element
Forces elements to display as inline boxes
Disables CSS margins completely
correctAnswer: Includes padding and border within the specified element width and height
explanation: With border-box, padding and borders do not expand the element beyond its declared width and height, simplifying layout math.

questionText: In Node.js, what is the role of `package.json`?
options: Manifest containing project metadata, script commands, and direct project dependencies
The compiled binary executable for Node
A database schema migration file
The web server configuration for Nginx
correctAnswer: Manifest containing project metadata, script commands, and direct project dependencies
explanation: package.json defines project details, execution scripts (e.g. npm start), and lists production and dev dependencies.

questionText: What does the SQL statement `SELECT u.name, o.total FROM users u LEFT JOIN orders o ON u.id = o.user_id;` return?
options: All users, including those who have placed no orders, with NULL in order columns
Only users who have placed at least one order
Only orders that belong to non-existent users
A cross product multiplying every user by every order
correctAnswer: All users, including those who have placed no orders, with NULL in order columns
explanation: LEFT JOIN preserves all rows from the left table (users); matching right table rows are joined, and non-matches populate NULL.

questionText: In React, what does the `useMemo` hook do?
options: Memoizes the computed result of an expensive calculation to avoid recalculating on every render
Stores component state in browser RAM permanently
Caches API responses from backend endpoints
Creates a reference to a DOM element
correctAnswer: Memoizes the computed result of an expensive calculation to avoid recalculating on every render
explanation: useMemo recomputes a memoized value only when one of its specified dependencies has changed.

questionText: What is the purpose of password hashing algorithms like BCrypt over standard SHA-256?
options: BCrypt incorporates a salt and an adaptive work factor (computational cost) to thwart brute-force and GPU attacks
BCrypt decrypts passwords faster when logging in
BCrypt converts passwords into plain text for verification
BCrypt requires no database storage
correctAnswer: BCrypt incorporates a salt and an adaptive work factor (computational cost) to thwart brute-force and GPU attacks
explanation: BCrypt is deliberately slow and salted, making rainbow table lookups and high-speed GPU cracking computationally intractable.

questionText: In React Router v6+, which component is used to define dynamic route matching and render matching route elements?
options: <Routes> and <Route>
<Switch> and <Router>
<NavigationContainer> and <Screen>
<Path> and <View>
correctAnswer: <Routes> and <Route>
explanation: In React Router v6, <Routes> wraps individual <Route path='...' element={<Component />} /> definitions.

questionText: What is an ORM (Object-Relational Mapping) library such as Hibernate or Prisma?
options: A tool that bridges object-oriented code and relational database tables, mapping classes to entities and methods to queries
A database server that stores JSON documents
A CSS preprocessor like SASS
A load balancer for HTTP traffic
correctAnswer: A tool that bridges object-oriented code and relational database tables, mapping classes to entities and methods to queries
explanation: ORMs map object-oriented domain models into relational SQL schemas, abstracting low-level SQL query generation and result mapping.

questionText: What is the purpose of the `useCallback` hook in React?
options: Returns a memoized version of a callback function that only changes when its dependencies change
Calls an API endpoint immediately on render
Creates a callback function that runs on a separate worker thread
Deletes unmounted components from memory
correctAnswer: Returns a memoized version of a callback function that only changes when its dependencies change
explanation: useCallback prevents unnecessary re-renders of memoized child components by preserving function identity between renders.

questionText: What does the HTTP header `Authorization: Bearer <token>` typically carry in modern web apps?
options: A signed JSON Web Token (JWT) representing verified user identity and claims
The user's plaintext password
The browser's version number
The server's IP address
correctAnswer: A signed JSON Web Token (JWT) representing verified user identity and claims
explanation: Bearer tokens carry compact credentials (like JWTs) in authorization headers to authenticate stateless REST API requests.

questionText: What are the three parts of a JSON Web Token (JWT)?
options: Header, Payload, and Signature
Username, Password, and Email
IP address, MAC address, and Port
Public key, Private key, and Certificate
correctAnswer: Header, Payload, and Signature
explanation: JWTs consist of base64url-encoded Header, Payload (claims), and cryptographic Signature separated by dots.

questionText: In CSS Grid, what does `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr));` create?
options: A responsive layout where columns automatically wrap and fill available row space with min width 250px
A fixed 3-column table
A single column that scrolls horizontally
A layout that only works on mobile screens
correctAnswer: A responsive layout where columns automatically wrap and fill available row space with min width 250px
explanation: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(...)) dynamically adjusts column count to container width without media queries.

questionText: What is 'Prop Drilling' in React?
options: Passing props through multiple intermediate components that do not need the data, merely to reach deeply nested children
Drilling holes into computer motherboards
Writing props with incorrect TypeScript types
Overriding props with state setters
correctAnswer: Passing props through multiple intermediate components that do not need the data, merely to reach deeply nested children
explanation: Prop drilling creates coupling across layers; mitigated using React Context, Zustand, or Redux state stores.

questionText: What does `git rebase main` do compared to `git merge main`?
options: Re-applies commits from the current branch on top of main's latest commit, creating a linear history
Deletes all commits on the current branch
Merges both branches and creates an explicit merge commit
Reverts all uncommitted changes in the working directory
correctAnswer: Re-applies commits from the current branch on top of main's latest commit, creating a linear history
explanation: Rebasing replays local commits on the tip of the target branch, producing clean, sequential project history.

questionText: What is the primary difference between SQL databases (PostgreSQL) and NoSQL document databases (MongoDB)?
options: SQL enforces structured schemas with ACID relational joins; document NoSQL stores schema-less JSON-like BSON documents
SQL can only store text; NoSQL can store numbers
NoSQL cannot be hosted in the cloud
SQL does not support primary keys
correctAnswer: SQL enforces structured schemas with ACID relational joins; document NoSQL stores schema-less JSON-like BSON documents
explanation: Relational databases excel at normalized relational schemas and strict transactions; document stores prioritize flexible, nested documents.

questionText: In REST architecture, what does 'Idempotence' mean?
options: Making multiple identical requests has the same outcome on server state as making a single request
The request completes in under 100 milliseconds
The endpoint requires administrative authorization
The request body must be empty
correctAnswer: Making multiple identical requests has the same outcome on server state as making a single request
explanation: GET, PUT, and DELETE are idempotent; repeating them multiple times results in the same resource state.

questionText: Which HTTP method is typically NOT idempotent?
options: POST
GET
PUT
DELETE
correctAnswer: POST
explanation: Submitting multiple identical POST requests typically creates multiple distinct resource entities.

questionText: What does the JavaScript `Array.prototype.reduce()` function do?
options: Executes a reducer callback on each element of the array, returning a single accumulated output value
Reduces array length by removing null items
Sorts array items in descending order
Filters elements matching a boolean predicate
correctAnswer: Executes a reducer callback on each element of the array, returning a single accumulated output value
explanation: reduce() iterates through array items, carrying an accumulator forward to produce a consolidated result.

questionText: What is 'Debouncing' in frontend user input handling?
options: Delaying execution of a function until a specified time has elapsed since the last time the event was triggered
Executing a function twice on every keystroke
Disabling buttons when forms are submitted
Converting strings to lowercase
correctAnswer: Delaying execution of a function until a specified time has elapsed since the last time the event was triggered
explanation: Debounce waits for user typing to pause (e.g. 300ms in search inputs) before firing expensive API requests.

questionText: What is 'Throttling' in web event handling?
options: Ensuring a function is called at most once within a specified time interval (e.g. on window scroll)
Slowing down internet connection speed
Canceling all background network requests
Reducing CPU usage to 10%
correctAnswer: Ensuring a function is called at most once within a specified time interval (e.g. on window scroll)
explanation: Throttling regulates execution frequency, executing callbacks at regular paced intervals during continuous events.

questionText: In Spring Boot, what is the role of `@Autowired` or constructor injection?
options: Injecting dependent bean instances automatically into managed classes via Dependency Injection (IoC)
Compiling Java bytecode into machine code
Validating form fields automatically
Opening database connections manually
correctAnswer: Injecting dependent bean instances automatically into managed classes via Dependency Injection (IoC)
explanation: Dependency injection decouples class creation from dependencies, injecting collaborating beans managed by Spring container.

questionText: What does `git stash` do?
options: Temporarily shelves uncommitted changes so you can work on a clean working copy, retrievable via `git stash pop`
Permanently deletes all modified files
Pushes code to GitHub immediately
Creates a new Git tag for release
correctAnswer: Temporarily shelves uncommitted changes so you can work on a clean working copy, retrievable via `git stash pop`
explanation: git stash records the current state of the working directory and index, resetting back to the HEAD commit.

questionText: What is a 'Pure Component' or pure function in React?
options: A component/function that returns the exact same JSX output for the same input props without side effects
A component written without using JSX
A component that has zero props
A component that never re-renders
correctAnswer: A component/function that returns the exact same JSX output for the same input props without side effects
explanation: Pure components compute output strictly from inputs, avoiding unpredictable mutations or hidden state.

questionText: What does the `@OneToMany(mappedBy = '...')` attribute in JPA specify?
options: Defines the inverse side of a bidirectional relationship, referencing the field in the child entity that owns the foreign key
Creates a new database table called one_to_many
Limits the query to only 1 row
Disables database transactions
correctAnswer: Defines the inverse side of a bidirectional relationship, referencing the field in the child entity that owns the foreign key
explanation: mappedBy tells Hibernate that the relationship is mapped by the opposing entity, preventing redundant join tables.

questionText: What is 'CORS Preflight' request in web browsers?
options: An automated HTTP OPTIONS request sent by browsers to verify server CORS permissions before sending non-simple requests
A test flight of an airplane
Checking internet bandwidth before downloading images
Validating HTML syntax before rendering
correctAnswer: An automated HTTP OPTIONS request sent by browsers to verify server CORS permissions before sending non-simple requests
explanation: Browsers send preflight OPTIONS requests for custom headers or non-simple methods (PUT/DELETE) to ensure server consent.

questionText: What is 'Content Security Policy' (CSP)?
options: An HTTP response header allowing site administrators to restrict resources (scripts, images, styles) browsers are allowed to load
A privacy policy displayed on a website footer
A security guard at a data center
A firewall configured on an operating system
correctAnswer: An HTTP response header allowing site administrators to restrict resources (scripts, images, styles) browsers are allowed to load
explanation: CSP mitigates XSS attacks by restricting authorized script sources and blocking inline execution.

questionText: What does the CSS property `z-index` control?
options: The stacking order of positioned elements along the z-axis (depth)
The zoom level of images
The horizontal alignment of text
The transparency of background colors
correctAnswer: The stacking order of positioned elements along the z-axis (depth)
explanation: z-index specifies layering priority for positioned elements (relative, absolute, fixed, sticky) within a stacking context.

questionText: In React, what is the difference between controlled and uncontrolled form inputs?
options: Controlled inputs have their value driven by React state; uncontrolled inputs store value in the DOM accessed via refs
Controlled inputs have validation; uncontrolled inputs do not
Controlled inputs only work on mobile devices
Uncontrolled inputs cannot be submitted
correctAnswer: Controlled inputs have their value driven by React state; uncontrolled inputs store value in the DOM accessed via refs
explanation: Controlled components bind input value to React state via onChange handlers, giving full programmatic control.

questionText: What does `npm install --save-dev <pkg>` (or `-D`) do?
options: Installs the package as a development dependency, excluded from production deployment bundles
Installs the package globally on the computer
Runs the package immediately in the terminal
Downloads source code without installing
correctAnswer: Installs the package as a development dependency, excluded from production deployment bundles
explanation: Dev dependencies (linters, test runners, build tools) are isolated from production runtime environments.

questionText: What is 'Lazy Loading' (React.lazy and dynamic import)?
options: Deferring component download until it is actually rendered on screen, splitting bundles into smaller chunks
Writing code slowly over several days
Delaying API responses by 5 seconds
Loading images only when clicked
correctAnswer: Deferring component download until it is actually rendered on screen, splitting bundles into smaller chunks
explanation: React.lazy() and import() enable code-splitting, downloading bundle chunks on demand to minimize initial page load times.

questionText: In SQL, what is an 'ACID' transaction?
options: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability: guarantees database transactions are processed reliably
A database query with multiple WHERE conditions
A syntax error in PostgreSQL
A method for encrypting database tables
correctAnswer: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability: guarantees database transactions are processed reliably
explanation: ACID guarantees: all-or-nothing changes (A), valid state constraints (C), isolated execution (I), and permanent persistence (D).

questionText: What does the `git cherry-pick <commit-hash>` command do?
options: Applies the changes from a specific existing commit onto the current working HEAD branch
Deletes a specific commit from history
Picks random files to delete
Pushes a branch to production
correctAnswer: Applies the changes from a specific existing commit onto the current working HEAD branch
explanation: cherry-pick copies a specific commit from one branch and commits it onto the currently active branch.

questionText: What is the purpose of the `useRef` hook in React?
options: Returns a mutable ref object whose .current property persists across renders without triggering a re-render when changed
Refreshes the page automatically
Fetches data from a REST API
Manages Redux store state
correctAnswer: Returns a mutable ref object whose .current property persists across renders without triggering a re-render when changed
explanation: useRef provides access to DOM nodes and holds mutable instance variables across render cycles without causing re-renders.

questionText: What is the 'Same-Origin Policy' (SOP) implemented by web browsers?
options: A critical security mechanism that prevents scripts on one origin from accessing sensitive resources on another origin
A rule requiring all web pages to use the same font
A law requiring websites to display cookie banners
A network policy that blocks all external links
correctAnswer: A critical security mechanism that prevents scripts on one origin from accessing sensitive resources on another origin
explanation: SOP isolates distinct origins (protocol + host + port), preventing malicious sites from reading authenticated data from others.

questionText: What is 'SQL Injection' (SQLi)?
options: An exploit where untrusted user input manipulates backend SQL queries due to unescaped string concatenation
Injecting database records using an automated script
Backing up a database using SQL scripts
Creating indexes on database columns
correctAnswer: An exploit where untrusted user input manipulates backend SQL queries due to unescaped string concatenation
explanation: SQL injection allows attackers to bypass authentication or extract sensitive database tables via malicious input parameters.

questionText: How do parameterized queries (PreparedStatement in Java / JPA) prevent SQL injection?
options: They treat user inputs strictly as literal data parameters, never parsing them as executable SQL commands
They encrypt the database server hard drive
They convert all input text into base64
They delete dangerous words like 'DROP' and 'SELECT'
correctAnswer: They treat user inputs strictly as literal data parameters, never parsing them as executable SQL commands
explanation: Prepared statements compile query templates first, binding inputs as raw literal values so structure cannot be altered.

questionText: In CSS, what is the 'Cascade' in Cascading Style Sheets?
options: The algorithm that resolves conflicts between multiple CSS rules based on origin, specificity, and source order
A waterfall animation in CSS
Applying styles to all child elements
Loading CSS files over HTTPS
correctAnswer: The algorithm that resolves conflicts between multiple CSS rules based on origin, specificity, and source order
explanation: The cascade resolves style conflicts using explicit hierarchy: importance (!important), specificity, and source declaration order.

questionText: What is 'Semantic HTML' and why is it important?
options: Using HTML tags that describe meaning (e.g. <header>, <nav>, <article>) for accessibility, SEO, and maintainability
Writing HTML without any CSS
Using only <div> and <span> tags
Writing HTML in alphabetical order
correctAnswer: Using HTML tags that describe meaning (e.g. <header>, <nav>, <article>) for accessibility, SEO, and maintainability
explanation: Semantic elements convey structural purpose to screen readers and search engines, creating accessible page hierarchies.

questionText: What is 'Server-Side Rendering' (SSR) compared to 'Client-Side Rendering' (CSR)?
options: SSR renders HTML on the server and delivers ready markup to browsers; CSR downloads JavaScript which builds DOM in browser
SSR requires no backend server
CSR loads faster on slow 2G internet connections
SSR works only on mobile phones
correctAnswer: SSR renders HTML on the server and delivers ready markup to browsers; CSR downloads JavaScript which builds DOM in browser
explanation: SSR delivers pre-rendered HTML for faster initial content paint and superior SEO indexing compared to pure client bundles.

questionText: What does `npm run build` typically produce in a modern Vite/React project?
options: A minified, bundled, and optimized production-ready `dist` folder containing HTML, JS, and CSS static assets
Starts a development hot-reloading server
Installs missing npm packages
Runs all automated unit tests
correctAnswer: A minified, bundled, and optimized production-ready `dist` folder containing HTML, JS, and CSS static assets
explanation: Vite compiles JSX/TypeScript, tree-shakes dead code, and minifies assets into static production bundles.

questionText: What is 'Tree Shaking' in modern JavaScript bundlers (Vite / Rollup / Webpack)?
options: Dead-code elimination that strips unused exports from the final JavaScript production bundle
Shaking computer hardware to test stability
Sorting files in alphabetical order in directories
Removing comments from CSS files
correctAnswer: Dead-code elimination that strips unused exports from the final JavaScript production bundle
explanation: Tree shaking uses ES6 static import/export analysis to omit unused functions and libraries from bundled code.

questionText: In Spring Boot, what does `@PathVariable` do in a controller method signature?
options: Extracts dynamic URI template variable values from the request path (e.g. `/users/{id}`)
Reads query parameters from the URL (?key=val)
Extracts JSON from the request body
Reads cookies from the HTTP header
correctAnswer: Extracts dynamic URI template variable values from the request path (e.g. `/users/{id}`)
explanation: @PathVariable binds URI placeholders (like {id}) directly to controller method parameter variables.

questionText: In Spring Boot, what does `@RequestParam` do?
options: Extracts query parameters or form data from the URL query string (e.g. `?page=1&size=10`)
Extracts path variables from the URI
Validates request headers
Extracts JWT tokens
correctAnswer: Extracts query parameters or form data from the URL query string (e.g. `?page=1&size=10`)
explanation: @RequestParam maps URL query parameters to method arguments, supporting optional defaults.

questionText: What is 'Database Normalization' (e.g. 1NF, 2NF, 3NF)?
options: Organizing database columns and tables to minimize redundant duplicate data and eliminate modification anomalies
Formatting numbers to two decimal places
Backing up database tables to cloud storage
Creating indexes on foreign keys
correctAnswer: Organizing database columns and tables to minimize redundant duplicate data and eliminate modification anomalies
explanation: Normalization structures relational schemas into distinct related tables, ensuring data integrity and consistency.

questionText: What is a 'Foreign Key' constraint in relational databases?
options: A column constraint enforcing referential integrity by ensuring values match primary keys in a referenced table
A key used to encrypt database backups
A primary key imported from an external database
A password used by database administrators
correctAnswer: A column constraint enforcing referential integrity by ensuring values match primary keys in a referenced table
explanation: Foreign keys prevent orphaned records by ensuring child table references correspond to valid parent records.

questionText: What is 'Virtual DOM' in React?
options: A lightweight in-memory JavaScript representation of the real DOM used to compute optimal updates via diffing
A 3D virtual reality interface in the browser
A headless Chrome browser instance
A copy of the database stored in RAM
correctAnswer: A lightweight in-memory JavaScript representation of the real DOM used to compute optimal updates via diffing
explanation: React renders to an in-memory Virtual DOM, diffing changes to apply minimal batch updates to the real browser DOM.

questionText: What is 'Reconciliation' in React?
options: The recursive diffing algorithm React uses to compare Virtual DOM trees and update the real browser DOM
Reconnecting a disconnected database
Reconciling credit card statements
Synchronizing Git branches
correctAnswer: The recursive diffing algorithm React uses to compare Virtual DOM trees and update the real browser DOM
explanation: Reconciliation determines what parts of the DOM changed between renders to minimize costly browser reflows.

questionText: What does the CSS property `flex-wrap: wrap;` do?
options: Allows flex items to wrap onto multiple lines if they exceed the container width
Forces all items onto a single line
Hides overflowing items from view
Animates items when hovering
correctAnswer: Allows flex items to wrap onto multiple lines if they exceed the container width
explanation: flex-wrap: wrap allows items that overflow the main axis to break cleanly onto new flex lines.

questionText: In JavaScript, what does `JSON.stringify()` do?
options: Converts a JavaScript object or value into a serialized JSON text string
Parses a JSON string into a JavaScript object
Validates whether a string is valid HTML
Encrypts objects using AES
correctAnswer: Converts a JavaScript object or value into a serialized JSON text string
explanation: JSON.stringify serializes in-memory objects into portable JSON string format.

questionText: In JavaScript, what does `JSON.parse()` do?
options: Parses a serialized JSON text string, constructing the JavaScript value or object described by the string
Converts objects to strings
Prints JSON to the terminal console
Compresses JSON files with gzip
correctAnswer: Parses a serialized JSON text string, constructing the JavaScript value or object described by the string
explanation: JSON.parse deserializes valid JSON strings into native JavaScript objects, arrays, and primitives.

questionText: What is the purpose of the `HTML5 <form>` tag's `event.preventDefault()` in React submit handlers?
options: Prevents the browser's default behavior of reloading the entire web page on form submission
Stops the form from submitting data
Clears all input values in the form
Submits the form directly to Google
correctAnswer: Prevents the browser's default behavior of reloading the entire web page on form submission
explanation: e.preventDefault() cancels standard browser page reloads, allowing React SPA code to handle submission via fetch/axios.

questionText: What is 'Destructuring Assignment' in JavaScript?
options: A syntax that allows unpacking values from arrays or properties from objects into distinct variables
Deleting object properties using the delete operator
Compiling JavaScript into WebAssembly
Splitting strings by commas
correctAnswer: A syntax that allows unpacking values from arrays or properties from objects into distinct variables
explanation: const { title, price } = course unpacks properties cleanly into local variables.

questionText: What is the 'Spread Operator' (`...`) in JavaScript used for?
options: Expanding iterable elements (arrays, objects) into individual elements or shallow copying object properties
Calculating math averages
Splitting long strings into paragraphs
Connecting two network sockets
correctAnswer: Expanding iterable elements (arrays, objects) into individual elements or shallow copying object properties
explanation: Spread ({ ...oldObj, newKey: val }) creates clean shallow copies with updated properties immutably.

questionText: In Spring Boot, how do you handle CORS globally across all controller endpoints?
options: By implementing `WebMvcConfigurer` and overriding `addCorsMappings(CorsRegistry registry)`
By adding `cors=true` in `application.properties`
By installing the CORS plugin in Chrome
By modifying the Windows firewall
correctAnswer: By implementing `WebMvcConfigurer` and overriding `addCorsMappings(CorsRegistry registry)`
explanation: WebMvcConfigurer allows setting allowed origins, methods, and headers across all API routes centralized in WebConfig.

questionText: What does HTTP Status Code `401 Unauthorized` signify?
options: The request lacks valid authentication credentials (e.g. missing or expired token)
The user is authenticated but lacks required permission roles
The requested resource was not found
The server crashed due to an exception
correctAnswer: The request lacks valid authentication credentials (e.g. missing or expired token)
explanation: 401 indicates authentication is required and has failed or has not been provided.

questionText: What does HTTP Status Code `403 Forbidden` signify?
options: The client is authenticated, but does not possess the permissions or authorization required for the resource
The client token is missing
The request syntax is malformed
The server is temporarily overloaded
correctAnswer: The client is authenticated, but does not possess the permissions or authorization required for the resource
explanation: 403 indicates the server understood the request and verified identity, but refuses authorization.

questionText: What does HTTP Status Code `404 Not Found` mean?
options: The server cannot locate a resource matching the requested Request-URI
The user password is incorrect
The request took too long to complete
The server is offline
correctAnswer: The server cannot locate a resource matching the requested Request-URI
explanation: 404 indicates the endpoint URI does not match any existing server route or entity record.

questionText: What does HTTP Status Code `500 Internal Server Error` mean?
options: The server encountered an unexpected condition or unhandled exception that prevented fulfilling the request
The user input failed validation
The database does not exist
The client disconnected early
correctAnswer: The server encountered an unexpected condition or unhandled exception that prevented fulfilling the request
explanation: 500 indicates an unhandled server-side crash or uncaught runtime exception occurred.

questionText: What is 'State Lifting' in React architecture?
options: Moving shared state up to the closest common ancestor component so siblings can coordinate
Uploading state to cloud storage
Converting component state into local variables
Deleting state when unmounting
correctAnswer: Moving shared state up to the closest common ancestor component so siblings can coordinate
explanation: Lifting state up shares single-source-of-truth state across multiple child components via props and callbacks.

questionText: What is 'Context API' in React?
options: A built-in mechanism to pass data through the component tree without manually passing props down every level
A tool for translating text into multiple languages
A database connection pool manager
A React hook for managing CSS animations
correctAnswer: A built-in mechanism to pass data through the component tree without manually passing props down every level
explanation: React.createContext and useContext allow broadcasting values (auth, theme) globally down component subtrees.

questionText: In PostgreSQL, what is a `SERIAL` or `BIGSERIAL` column type?
options: An auto-incrementing integer sequence commonly used for primary keys
A column for storing serial numbers of hardware
A column that stores serialized JSON strings
An encrypted binary column
correctAnswer: An auto-incrementing integer sequence commonly used for primary keys
explanation: SERIAL creates an auto-incrementing integer sequence default, generating sequential numeric primary keys automatically.

questionText: What is a 'Database Migration' tool (Flyway / Liquibase)?
options: A version control tool that tracks, manages, and applies incremental SQL schema changes predictably across environments
Moving physical database servers between offices
Exporting database tables into Excel spreadsheets
Converting PostgreSQL into MySQL
correctAnswer: A version control tool that tracks, manages, and applies incremental SQL schema changes predictably across environments
explanation: Migration tools apply versioned DDL scripts sequentially, keeping schema revisions in lockstep with codebase versions.

questionText: What does the CSS pseudo-class `:hover` do?
options: Applies styles to an element when the user points to it with a cursor or mouse
Applies styles when an element is clicked
Applies styles when an input is focused
Applies styles only on mobile screens
correctAnswer: Applies styles to an element when the user points to it with a cursor or mouse
explanation: :hover enables micro-interactions by transforming appearances (colors, transforms) when cursors hover.

questionText: What does the CSS pseudo-class `:focus-visible` do?
options: Applies focus indicators (rings, outlines) only when keyboard navigation warrants focus visibility
Hides elements from screen readers
Makes invisible elements visible
Zooms elements on click
correctAnswer: Applies focus indicators (rings, outlines) only when keyboard navigation warrants focus visibility
explanation: :focus-visible provides clean accessible focus rings for keyboard tab users while omitting them on mouse clicks.

questionText: What is the 'Box Model' in CSS consisting of, from inside out?
options: Content, Padding, Border, Margin
Margin, Border, Padding, Content
Border, Margin, Content, Padding
Padding, Content, Border, Margin
correctAnswer: Content, Padding, Border, Margin
explanation: The box model wraps every HTML element in layers: inner Content, internal Padding, enclosing Border, and external Margin.

questionText: What does `git status` show in the command line?
options: The state of the working directory and staging area, highlighting modified, untracked, and staged files
The battery status of the computer
The internet upload and download speed
The version of Git installed on the computer
correctAnswer: The state of the working directory and staging area, highlighting modified, untracked, and staged files
explanation: git status details modified tracked files, staged changes ready for commit, and new untracked files.

questionText: What does `git pull` do?
options: Fetches commits from a remote repository and immediately integrates/merges them into the current local branch
Pushes local commits to the remote repository
Deletes remote branches
Pulls changes into a stash
correctAnswer: Fetches commits from a remote repository and immediately integrates/merges them into the current local branch
explanation: git pull combines git fetch (downloading remote objects) and git merge (integrating into the local HEAD).

questionText: What is 'Tree Traversal' in DOM manipulation?
options: Navigating parent, child, and sibling nodes within the hierarchical document object model tree
Traversing tree structures in binary search trees
Climbing trees in computer graphics games
Scanning folders on a hard drive
correctAnswer: Navigating parent, child, and sibling nodes within the hierarchical document object model tree
explanation: DOM traversal navigates relations (parentElement, children, nextElementSibling) to inspect or modify elements.

questionText: What is the difference between synchronous and asynchronous code execution in JavaScript?
options: Synchronous code blocks thread execution until complete; asynchronous code delegates tasks and continues execution
Synchronous code runs in parallel on 8 threads; asynchronous code runs on 1 thread
Synchronous code is faster than asynchronous code
Asynchronous code cannot be used in web browsers
correctAnswer: Synchronous code blocks thread execution until complete; asynchronous code delegates tasks and continues execution
explanation: JavaScript's single thread avoids blocking on I/O by delegating async operations to the browser runtime and event loop.

questionText: What does `async/await` syntax provide in JavaScript?
options: Syntactic sugar over Promises that allows writing asynchronous code with sequential, readable synchronous-like flow
A way to run code on background threads in C++
An alternative to HTML form tags
A CSS animation library
correctAnswer: Syntactic sugar over Promises that allows writing asynchronous code with sequential, readable synchronous-like flow
explanation: async functions return Promises, and await pauses execution until the awaited Promise resolves cleanly.

questionText: What is 'REST' (Representational State Transfer)?
options: An architectural style for designing networked web APIs using standard HTTP verbs, statelessness, and resource URIs
A Java library for connecting to databases
A command-line tool for restarting servers
A CSS layout framework like Bootstrap
correctAnswer: An architectural style for designing networked web APIs using standard HTTP verbs, statelessness, and resource URIs
explanation: REST defines architectural constraints (stateless, client-server, cacheable, uniform interface) for interoperable web services.

questionText: What does the `@Column(unique = true)` annotation in JPA enforce?
options: A database UNIQUE constraint preventing duplicate column values across table rows
That the column can only be updated once
That only one user can read the column
That the column value must be a UUID
correctAnswer: A database UNIQUE constraint preventing duplicate column values across table rows
explanation: unique = true adds a UNIQUE DDL constraint in relational tables, throwing integrity exceptions on duplicates.

questionText: What is 'CascadeType.ALL' in JPA entity relationships?
options: Cascades all persistence lifecycle operations (PERSIST, MERGE, REMOVE, REFRESH, DETACH) from parent to child entities
Deletes all tables in the database
Runs queries on all database nodes
Cascades CSS styles down all child elements
correctAnswer: Cascades all persistence lifecycle operations (PERSIST, MERGE, REMOVE, REFRESH, DETACH) from parent to child entities
explanation: CascadeType.ALL ensures child entities are automatically persisted, updated, or deleted alongside their parent entity.

questionText: What does `orphanRemoval = true` in JPA `@OneToMany` achieve?
options: Automatically deletes child entity rows from the database if they are dereferenced or removed from the parent's collection
Deletes parent entities if they have no children
Removes unused columns from database tables
Kills orphaned backend server processes
correctAnswer: Automatically deletes child entity rows from the database if they are dereferenced or removed from the parent's collection
explanation: orphanRemoval ensures child records unlinked from parent collections are automatically issued SQL DELETE commands.

questionText: What is the purpose of `@JsonIgnore` in Jackson / Spring Boot?
options: Excludes the annotated property or field from JSON serialization and deserialization
Ignores JSON formatting syntax errors
Deletes JSON files from the server
Converts JSON into XML
correctAnswer: Excludes the annotated property or field from JSON serialization and deserialization
explanation: @JsonIgnore prevents sensitive fields (passwords) or circular relationship collections from serializing into response JSON.

questionText: What is 'Circular Reference' in Jackson JSON serialization?
options: When entity A references entity B, and B references A, causing infinite recursion during JSON serialization
When a database query has a recursive CTE
When a JavaScript function calls itself infinitely
When two CSS rules reference each other
correctAnswer: When entity A references entity B, and B references A, causing infinite recursion during JSON serialization
explanation: Bidirectional JPA entities create infinite recursive serialization loops unless broken by @JsonIgnore or @JsonManagedReference.

questionText: What is 'CORS' (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing)?
options: A browser security mechanism that restricts web applications on one origin from requesting resources from another origin
A database replication protocol
A CSS responsive layout technique
A Git branch merging strategy
correctAnswer: A browser security mechanism that restricts web applications on one origin from requesting resources from another origin
explanation: CORS prevents malicious cross-origin scripts from making unauthorized requests to internal API services.

questionText: What is 'JWT Statelessness' and why is it beneficial for scalable web backends?
options: Servers verify user sessions mathematically using cryptographic signatures without needing session storage in memory or databases
Tokens are completely unencrypted and public
Servers do not verify user permissions
Sessions never expire
correctAnswer: Servers verify user sessions mathematically using cryptographic signatures without needing session storage in memory or databases
explanation: Stateless JWT verification scales across distributed microservice instances without requiring shared session cache lookups.

questionText: What does `npm audit` do?
options: Scans installed npm package dependencies for known security vulnerabilities recorded in the vulnerability database
Audits company financial records
Checks that code compiles without warnings
Counts the total lines of code in the project
correctAnswer: Scans installed npm package dependencies for known security vulnerabilities recorded in the vulnerability database
explanation: npm audit analyzes dependency trees against CVE security advisory databases, reporting known security flaws.

questionText: What is 'Responsive Web Design'?
options: Designing web applications that dynamically adapt layout, typography, and elements smoothly across any device screen width
Making websites that load in under 1 second
A website that sends automated email responses
An app that speaks to the user using voice
correctAnswer: Designing web applications that dynamically adapt layout, typography, and elements smoothly across any device screen width
explanation: Responsive design uses fluid grids, flexible images, and media queries to deliver great UX on mobile, tablet, and desktop.

questionText: What is 'Flexbox' in CSS designed for?
options: One-dimensional layout alignment and space distribution among items along a row or column axis
Two-dimensional grid layouts with columns and rows
3D web animations with WebGL
Responsive typography font scaling
correctAnswer: One-dimensional layout alignment and space distribution among items along a row or column axis
explanation: CSS Flexbox provides layout models for aligning items along a single axis (either row or column).

questionText: What is 'CSS Grid' designed for?
options: Two-dimensional layouts allowing precise positioning of items across both rows and columns simultaneously
One-dimensional linear layouts
Styling forms and buttons
Drawing vector icons
correctAnswer: Two-dimensional layouts allowing precise positioning of items across both rows and columns simultaneously
explanation: CSS Grid is a two-dimensional layout system that manages both horizontal columns and vertical rows simultaneously.

questionText: What is 'Media Query' in CSS (`@media (max-width: 768px)`)?
options: A CSS rule that applies style blocks conditionally based on device viewport capabilities and screen widths
A query that plays video and audio files
A database query for media files
An API call that downloads images
correctAnswer: A CSS rule that applies style blocks conditionally based on device viewport capabilities and screen widths
explanation: Media queries evaluate viewport dimensions, applying targeted style overrides for smaller mobile and tablet viewports.

questionText: What is 'Local Storage' in modern browsers?
options: A persistent client-side key-value storage mechanism with ~5MB quota that survives browser restarts
A temporary cookie that expires in 10 minutes
A local file on the user's desktop
A database hosted on localhost
correctAnswer: A persistent client-side key-value storage mechanism with ~5MB quota that survives browser restarts
explanation: localStorage stores string key-value pairs persistently across browser tabs and sessions until programmatically cleared.

questionText: What is 'Session Storage' in modern browsers?
options: A client-side key-value storage mechanism whose data is purged when the specific browser tab is closed
Storage that lasts for 1 year
A database on the backend server
A file stored in the cloud
correctAnswer: A client-side key-value storage mechanism whose data is purged when the specific browser tab is closed
explanation: sessionStorage stores data strictly for the duration of a single browser tab session, clearing upon tab closure.

questionText: What is 'Tree-Walking' in Git commit history?
options: Navigating the directed acyclic graph (DAG) of commit snapshots using parent commit hashes
Scanning directories on a hard drive
Merging two unrelated Git repositories
Deleting unreferenced Git objects with prune
correctAnswer: Navigating the directed acyclic graph (DAG) of commit snapshots using parent commit hashes
explanation: Git represents commit history as a DAG of immutable snapshots; traversing parent pointers reconstructs history.

questionText: What is 'Cross-Origin Resource Sharing' (CORS) preflight caching using `Access-Control-Max-Age`?
options: Specifies how many seconds the results of a preflight OPTIONS request can be cached by the browser
Caches all API responses in the browser for 1 year
Sets the maximum size of uploaded files
Limits the maximum age of users
correctAnswer: Specifies how many seconds the results of a preflight OPTIONS request can be cached by the browser
explanation: Access-Control-Max-Age reduces latency by instructing browsers to cache preflight responses for the specified duration.

questionText: What is the fundamental philosophy of Full Stack Engineering?
options: Building cohesive end-to-end digital experiences from intuitive user interfaces down to resilient backend systems and databases
Writing only backend code and ignoring UI design
Focusing exclusively on CSS styling
Delegating all database queries to third parties
correctAnswer: Building cohesive end-to-end digital experiences from intuitive user interfaces down to resilient backend systems and databases
explanation: Full stack engineering integrates UX, frontend state, API contracts, backend logic, and database schemas holistically.
